judge_assessment.explanation: Every mathematical claim the judge made holds and I re-derived all of it: 3^2 - 4(3) + 7 = 4; (x^2-2x-3)/(x-3) = x+1 -> 4 with 2 the mis-cancellation trap; the conjugate gives 1/(sqrt(x+4)+2) -> 1/4 with 1/2 the drop-the-plus-2 trap; 1/(x-2) -> -inf from the left and +inf from the right; |x|/x -> -1 and +1; (x-7)/(x-4) -> +inf from the LEFT and -inf from the right, because the numerator is near -3; and 9 + k = 14 gives k = 5 with common value 14, the trap k = 14 leaving a jump of 9. verify.json encodes each of these with explicit 'dir' fields for the one-sided cases, and all three declared traps carry values so the Common wrong answers block renders. Where I disagree is the judge's implicit acceptance of one manual item on an error-analysis sheet. Problems 4, 5, 6 and 7 are all headed 'Find and fix the mistake' and each demands written diagnosis — 'state what the two-sided limit is and why', 'explain what the student's rule left out' — and the worksheet directions make it a requirement for every such item: 'quote the line of the student's reasoning that fails, then redo the problem from that line on.' None of those four has a manual entry; verify.json declares manual only for id 8. Problem 1 likewise asks the student to 'state in one line why direct substitution is legitimate here' with nothing recorded. So the sheet whose entire purpose is diagnosis records exactly one diagnosis as needing a human reader. Two smaller printed defects also went unreported: the Quick Answers row for problem 3 reads '3. 1/4, 0.25' on a problem whose stem says 'Give the exact value, not a decimal approximation' (verify.json id 3's second entry declares expected 0.25 rather than '1/4'), and problem 2's row reads '2. 4, 4' because the supporting check on the simplified form x+1 is banked beside the limit itself, so a one-answer problem prints two identical answers.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 6 is the sharpest item in the batch because it defeats the student's rule with the numerator rather than the denominator: (x-7)/(x-4) has numerator near -3 at x = 4, so the LEFT limit is +inf and the RIGHT is -inf — the reverse of the naive expectation. The key states the procedure that generalises it: 'two signs, then one division: sign of the numerator at the point, sign of the denominator on that side', then names the exact scope of the student's error — 'The student's rule happens to be right only when the numerator is positive.'

The four find-and-fix items are graded by kind of failure, not by difficulty alone: an infinite limit whose sides disagree (4), a finite jump from an absolute value (5), a sign error driven by the numerator (6), and a parameter question answered with the wrong quantity (7). The key names each wrong answer's origin — for problem 7, '14 is the value of the right-hand branch at x = 3; k is a constant sitting inside the left-hand branch'.

The one-sided verification is encoded properly rather than approximated: verify.json ids 4, 5 and 6 each carry two limit entries with explicit 'dir': '-' and 'dir': '+' and expecteds '-oo'/'oo', so the machine record distinguishes the two sides the way the worksheet asks the student to.

The directions distinguish the two ways a limit can fail to be a number — 'Write infinity or -infinity where the limit is infinite, and write does not exist where the two sides disagree — those are different statements' — and the key holds that line in problem 4 ('Writing infinity for it is a stronger claim than the function supports') and problem 8 ('Writing infinity would claim the function grows without bound on both sides, which is a description of a different graph').

Problem 8's manual desc is written as a reviewer checklist rather than a restatement: it requires 0/0 to be called indeterminate rather than undefined, at least one named algebraic route, and per-side sign analysis instead of the assumption that the right side gives +inf.

root_causes.description: On a worksheet whose instructional mode is misconception analysis, the written diagnosis is the assessed work, and none of it is declared. Problems 4, 5, 6 and 7 each require the student to quote and correct a line of faulty reasoning; the verify entries capture only the numeric limits those items also produce, so the pipeline records four diagnosis items as fully machine-verified and reports one open response.
evidence: worksheet.pdf directions: 'On every find-and-fix item, quote the line of the student's reasoning that fails, then redo the problem from that line on.'
worksheet.pdf problem 6: 'Determine both one-sided limits at x = 4 and explain what the student's rule left out.' verify.json id 6: two limit entries, no manual entry.
worksheet.pdf problem 1: 'state in one line why direct substitution is legitimate here.' verify.json id 1: a single limit entry.
verify.json declares exactly one manual entry, id 8; the judge reviewed one manual item.

root_causes.description: The Quick Answers bank prints every entry that has an 'expected', with no distinction between the answer a student writes and a supporting check on an intermediate form. That produces a decimal on a problem that forbids decimals (id 3's second entry declares 0.25 where the answer is 1/4) and a duplicated row where one answer exists (id 2's limit 4 plus the simplified-form eval 4, printed '4, 4').
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 3: 'Give the exact value, not a decimal approximation.' answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '3. 1/4, 0.25'.
verify.json id 2 entries: limit -> 4 and {'type': 'eval', 'expr': 'x + 1', 'expected': 4}; answer_key.pdf prints '2. 4, 4'.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry(): 'vals = [e["expected"] for e in entries if ... "expected" in e]' — no notion of which entry is the answer.

improvements.title: Declare the written diagnosis in find-and-fix problems 4, 5, 6, 7 (and problem 1's justification) as manual items
improvements.proposed_change: Make the misconception-analysis mode require, for every find-and-fix item, a manual entry whose desc states what the diagnosis must contain — for problem 6 that would be 'names that the numerator is negative near x = 4, so the left-hand quotient is positive and the right-hand quotient negative; states that the student's rule assumes a positive numerator'. Numeric limits stay machine-checked; the sentence gets a declared acceptance criterion. Generate the manual count in final_response.md from verify.json so a diagnosis-focused sheet cannot report one open item out of five.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with curr-454's worksheet source and verify.json: the gate must exit non-zero listing problems 1, 4, 5, 6 and 7 as explanation or diagnosis slots with no manual entry, while problem 8 passes. Adding manual entries with descs makes the fixture pass and the generated manual count read six.
improvements.expected_impact: Aligns the machine record with what the worksheet actually assesses. On misconception-analysis tasks the diagnosis is the learning objective, and recording it as machine-verified both misstates the grading burden and removes the step where the author would have to write down what a correct diagnosis says.
improvements.risk: Find-and-fix items pair a short written diagnosis with fully checkable arithmetic; flagging them identically to full open synthesis (problem 8) will overstate grading time unless the manual list distinguishes the two, and could discourage authors from including find-and-fix items at all.

improvements.title: Stop the bank printing 0.25 on a problem that requires the exact value
improvements.proposed_change: Require an entry's 'expected' to be written in the form the stem requests — here '1/4' rather than 0.25 for id 3's supporting check — and add a gate rule: when a stem contains 'exact value', 'exact fraction' or 'not a decimal', no entry for that problem may declare a float expected, and the bank may not print a decimal for it. Keep the numeric tolerance machinery for checking; it is the PRINTED form that must follow the stem.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with curr-454's problem 3 stem ('Give the exact value, not a decimal approximation') and its current verify entries; the gate must exit non-zero naming the float expected 0.25. Changing that entry's expected to '1/4' makes it pass and the rendered row reads '3. 1/4'.
improvements.expected_impact: The delivered key stops contradicting its own worksheet on answer form. A student marked against '0.25' on a problem that forbade decimals is being graded against the opposite of the instruction.
improvements.risk: Some problems legitimately want both forms shown (an exact value plus a decimal for interpretation); the rule must be driven by the stem's own wording so those cases are unaffected.

improvements.title: Distinguish answer entries from supporting checks so a one-answer problem does not print '4, 4'
improvements.proposed_change: Add a per-entry 'role' field ('answer' by default, 'support' for checks on intermediate forms) to the verify schema. scripts/render_quick_answers.py banks only 'answer' entries, so problem 2 prints '2. 4' rather than '4, 4' while the simplified-form check on x+1 still runs and still anchors its trap. The same field fixes the mirror-image defect elsewhere in the run, where intermediate counts are banked and the composed answer the student must write is not.
improvements.regression_test: Feed render_quick_answers.py curr-454's verify.json with the second id-2 entry marked role 'support' and assert row 2 renders '4' exactly once; without the field, today's renderer produces '4, 4', so the assertion fails before the change and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Every bank row states one value per printed answer slot, which is what makes the bank usable for fast grading. Removes the duplicate-answer confusion here and, applied across the run, stops verification bookkeeping from appearing in the teacher's answer column.
improvements.risk: Defaulting to 'answer' preserves current behaviour but means the improvement only takes effect where authors mark supports, so the coverage gate must be the thing that forces the marking — otherwise the field is optional and unused.

case_summary: A precise, well-targeted limits error-analysis sheet that deserves its ACCEPT on mathematics: I confirmed all fourteen checks, including the one that matters most — (x-7)/(x-4) has a NEGATIVE numerator at x = 4, so the left-hand limit is +inf and the right-hand is -inf, exactly reversing the rule the fictional student states — and the one-sided entries are encoded with explicit 'dir' fields rather than approximated. Three traps carry values and render. What the judge did not report is that a misconception-analysis worksheet whose directions require the student to 'quote the line of the student's reasoning that fails' declares only one manual item: problems 4, 5, 6 and 7 all require written diagnosis and all are recorded as fully machine-verified. Two printed nits sit alongside it, both from the bank printing every entry with an expected: problem 3's row is '1/4, 0.25' on a stem that forbids decimals, and problem 2's row is '4, 4' because a supporting check on the simplified form is banked as a second answer.
